title: Choose public project name and branding
description:
## Decision
Select the public repository, binary, application display name, and compatibility subtitle before GitHub publication. The decision is pending user acceptance; current recommendation is gamedacctl.

## Rationale
gamedacctl is immediately discoverable to Linux users, follows a familiar ctl naming convention, currently has no GitHub search collision, and appears less vendor-official than steelseries-gamedac-linux.

## Alternatives Considered
GlowDAC is a more neutral and polished brand but is less searchable and may be mistaken for an audio-DAC project. LumenDAC has the same ambiguity. Retaining steelseries-gamedac-linux is explicit locally but visually resembles a vendor-owned repository and is unnecessarily long for a binary name.
design: Prefer gamedacctl because it is discoverable, Unix-native, currently absent from GitHub search, and the ctl suffix reduces official-product ambiguity. Do not rename the local checkout or create a GitHub repository until the user accepts the name.
acceptance_criteria: Name is checked in the intended GitHub namespace, receives a basic package/web/trademark collision review, uses original artwork, and is documented with an independent-project compatibility disclaimer.
close_reason: Accepted gamedacctl for repository, package, binary, and future app; public namespace and crates.io collision checks passed; explicit unofficial compatibility disclaimer added; no artwork currently shipped.

title: Resolve animated header and generate Breathe packets
description: Determine the role of animated header RGB offsets 2-4, reproduce known Breathe packets from structured inputs, then verify one new color and duration plus connected Sweep, Synchronized, and reverse behavior.
design: Follow every exact-capture, exact-generation, new-combination, and product-promotion gate in docs/research-process.md.
acceptance_criteria: Generated known cases match captures byte-for-byte; one new case is physically verified with static rollback; unknown Reflected or ColorShift semantics remain fail-closed.
close_reason: Generated Breathe/Sweep reports match eight GG fixtures byte-for-byte; new Synchronized and Sweep cases physically verified with static rollback; reverse flag reproduced with visual-direction ambiguity documented; unsupported effects remain fail-closed.

title: Replace root execution with scoped device access
description: Provide a narrow, reviewable udev-based access path for GameDAC 1038:1280 interface 0 so the CLI and GUI never invoke sudo or require a privileged daemon.
design: Prefer TAG+=uaccess or an equivalently narrow supported mechanism. Do not grant broad hidraw access.
acceptance_criteria: An active desktop user can control only the intended HID interface without root; reconnect works; audio device 1038:1282 remains available; permission removal has a documented rollback.
notes: Installed the exact source-controlled udev rule and verified live scope: only 1038:1280 interface 00 receives uaccess and the active-user ACL; interfaces 01/02 and 1038:1282 interface 05 remain excluded. Rule-removal plus logical reconnect removed access and caused gamedacctl to fail closed with Permission denied. Reinstall plus logical reconnect restored access automatically. A final manual upstream-cable disconnect/reconnect produced full remove/add events for both products; interface 00 regained access, non-root four-zone static control succeeded, the default six-channel sink returned at 60 percent, and the user heard spoken audio. Note: even a control-only authorization cycle briefly resets the audio sibling.
close_reason: Scoped non-root access, exclusion boundaries, fail-closed removal rollback, logical reconnect, manual cable reconnect, controller recovery, and GameDAC audio recovery were all verified.

title: Implement safe controller core and CLI
description: Create a typed packet and transport boundary for verified static earcup and microphone controls, off, exact captured presets, validation, and dry-run output without claiming unsupported effects.
design: Keep packet builders pure and transport separate. Retain the Python research utility as executable reference during migration.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests cover every byte and zone mask; malformed and unsupported inputs fail closed; verified commands preserve GameDAC audio and have physical acceptance evidence.
notes: Implemented native Rust packet/core/CLI boundary with static earcup and microphone zones, explicit off targets, guarded exact-pcap replay, HID interface selection, dry-run output, 12 passing tests, strict clippy, and documentation. Added exact SHA-256 regression checks for known Sweep, Synchronized, and five-second Breathe reports. Pending: install scoped udev rule, physically verify Rust static/mic/off/replay writes, reconnect behavior, and unchanged 1038:1282 audio before closure.
close_reason: Implemented and physically accepted the non-root Rust controller core: deterministic packet fixtures, fail-closed validation, independent earcup and microphone colors, every off target, exact Synchronized replay, and preserved GameDAC 5.1 audio.

title: Build native GameDAC Linux controller
description: Deliver the standalone Linux lighting controller and optional Omarchy integration defined in docs/app-plan.md while preserving Linux audio and the documented safety boundary.
design: docs/app-plan.md is the canonical architecture and milestone specification. docs/research-process.md governs protocol promotion. docs/legal.md governs publication boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: All child work required for the chosen release scope is complete; supported behavior is physically verified; packaging and publication safeguards are satisfied.

title: Prepare legally cautious public release
description: Choose original branding and an open-source license, document compatibility and experimental boundaries, produce reproducible Arch packaging, and review all distributed material against docs/legal.md.
design: Use SteelSeries marks only descriptively. Generated protocol code, not GG components or captured packets, must power release binaries.
acceptance_criteria: Release includes independent-project disclaimer, compatibility matrix, original assets, no proprietary files or raw whole-bus captures, reviewed udev access, and legal review before any commercial distribution.

title: Add thin Omarchy shell adapter
description: Provide an optional Omarchy bar widget and panel for device status and profile selection without placing USB, packet, polling, or privilege logic inside omarchy-shell.
design: Distribute as a separate manifest-root plugin repository after the native controller interface is stable.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin manifest validates; enable, reload, and removal work; controller failure cannot destabilize omarchy-shell; the plugin communicates only through the stable native API.

title: Build native desktop UI and profiles
description: Build a portable Linux GUI and profile model over the stable controller core with explicit device, permission, disconnected, and write-result states.
design: Prefer GTK4/libadwaita for the native UI and add D-Bus only when front-end serialization or reconnect persistence requires it.
acceptance_criteria: No root prompt; profile persistence survives restart; reconnect policy is opt-in; all exposed controls map only to verified core features; Linux audio is unchanged.

title: Select among multiple connected GameDACs
description:
## Problem
The controller currently selects the first matching 1038:1280 interface 0. That is convenient for the normal single-device case but ambiguous if more than one identical original GameDAC is connected.

## Scope
Enumerate matching compatible devices, preserve zero-configuration behavior when exactly one exists, and provide an explicit CLI/application selector when multiple matches exist. Refuse all writes while selection is ambiguous.
design: Use verified VID/PID/interface/report characteristics as the compatibility boundary. Prefer a device serial as the durable selector when exposed; otherwise present a clearly labeled physical/sysfs path with documented reconnect limitations. Never guess or silently choose the first device when multiple compatible units are present.
acceptance_criteria: One matching GameDAC continues to work without a selector; zero devices reports not found; multiple matches list distinguishable choices and fail closed until one is selected; tests cover enumeration and selection without hardware; the selected transport cannot open a different match; GUI/profile implications are documented.
